data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 defines its forbidden case over the refusal in requirement (1) only — it establishes that `LEASE_MISMATCH` must not mutate to a generic 500 — but it never authors any forbidden case, scratch note, or fixture element for requirement (2): the school-to-seat binding whose endpoint identity disagrees with the frozen seat must not be counted as coverage. The problem explicitly demands that the suite cover BOTH untested refusals, and the deliverable is judged on whether EACH forbidden case names a mutation that would today pass silently. Because SRC_001 is scoped entirely to the lease-mismatch / pre-provider-call refusal, it leaves the coverage-counting mutation (e.g., a suite that silently passes when a mismatched school-to-seat binding is still tallied as covered) unnamed and unprotected. The single-difference mutation principle is carried over into SRC_002 via the analogy, but that does not repair SRC_001's own omission: its own claim and mechanism address only the typed-code ejection site, leaving the false-green risk on the coverage side without a corresponding machine-checkable forbidden case. This is a direct failure of the problem's 'two untested refusals' requirement as applied to this target.
